distillation_scope: Pure disease-name leaf distillation for the full clinical spectrum of nocardiosis. Pulmonary, CNS, cutaneous, disseminated, transplant, steroid, TNF inhibitor, and other host contexts are represented as mechanisms, axes, risk factors, and treatment modifiers rather than disease-name qualifiers.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Exposure to soil, dust, decaying vegetation, water, traumatic skin inoculation, or rare healthcare environmental contamination supplies the organism. Inhalation usually seeds lung disease; direct inoculation can seed primary cutaneous disease.

Defective macrophage, neutrophil, and T-cell control from solid organ transplant immunosuppression, glucocorticoids, malignancy therapy, HIV, diabetes, chronic lung disease, pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, or advanced age permits invasive disease and dissemination.
Aerosolized Nocardia reaches bronchioles and alveoli, producing pneumonia, nodules, masses, cavitary lesions, pleural involvement, or a chronic TB- or malignancy-like lung process.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Intracellular survival and suppurative granulomatous infection
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Branching aerobic actinomycetes survive intracellularly and drive neutrophilic suppuration with abscesses, granulomatous inflammation, slow culture growth, and relapse when antimicrobial exposure or drainage is insufficient.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Nodular, mass-like, or cavitary pulmonary infection
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Pulmonary organism burden and suppuration produce multifocal consolidation, nodules, mass-like lesions, cavitation, lung abscess, pleural effusion, cough, hemoptysis, and hypoxemia. Imaging may resemble malignancy, tuberculosis, fungal disease, or septic emboli.

From pulmonary, cutaneous, or occult primary sites, Nocardia can disseminate through blood to brain, skin, soft tissue, kidney, bone, eye, heart, or other organs. Dissemination is enriched by impaired cellular immunity and delayed active therapy.

Disseminated organisms seed brain parenchyma, forming solitary or multiple ring-enhancing abscesses with headache, nausea, focal deficits, seizure, altered mental status, mass effect, recurrence, and high mortality if diagnosis, drainage, or CNS-active therapy is delayed.
Direct inoculation or dissemination produces cellulitis, ulcers, nodules, papulopustules, draining abscesses, mycetoma-like disease, or lymphocutaneous spread.

Host response to invasive pulmonary or disseminated Nocardia produces fever, night sweats, fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, leukocytosis or neutrophilia, CRP elevation, and sepsis-like physiology in severe disease. Immunosuppression may blunt fever or inflammatory markers.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Inactive therapy, resistance, and relapse pathway
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Species-level susceptibility variation, sulfonamide intolerance, poor CNS penetration, monotherapy for severe disease, retained abscess cavities, and short courses allow progression or recurrence despite nonspecific antibacterial exposure.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Inhalation is the usual entry route for pulmonary nocardiosis.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Requires traumatic inoculation or contaminated wound exposure.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Direct inoculation can cause primary cutaneous nocardiosis.
Impaired cellular and phagocyte control permits persistent intracellular survival and abscess formation.
Pulmonary seeding becomes invasive when organisms persist in local tissue and macrophages.
Suppurative lung infection produces nodules, masses, abscesses, and cavitation.
Tissue-invasive organism burden drives fever, leukocytosis, CRP elevation, and constitutional symptoms.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Amplified by immunosuppression, high burden, delayed diagnosis, or inactive therapy.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Persistent invasive infection can seed distant organs hematogenously.
Brain is a common and high-risk site of disseminated nocardiosis.
Skin and soft tissue can be seeded during disseminated disease even without direct inoculation.
Inactive or poorly penetrating therapy permits ongoing organism survival.
Airway irritation and pneumonia produce cough.
Necrotizing or cavitary pulmonary lesions can produce blood-streaked sputum or hemoptysis.
Pulmonary infiltrates, pleural disease, and oxygenation impairment cause dyspnea.
Airspace infection and pleural involvement lower oxygenation in severe pulmonary nocardiosis.
Pulmonary nocardiosis commonly appears as pneumonia or consolidation.
Nodules are a common CT expression of pulmonary nocardiosis.
Suppurative necrosis can cavitate pulmonary nodules or masses.
Pulmonary nocardiosis can mimic lung malignancy with infiltrating masses or PET-avid lesions.
Parapneumonic pleural effusion can accompany pulmonary nocardiosis.
Fever is common but can be absent or blunted in chronic or immunosuppressed disease.
Tachycardia can accompany fever, systemic inflammation, hypoxemia, or sepsis-like nocardiosis.
A history of subjective or recurrent fever can be more informative than a single triage temperature.
Subacute pulmonary nocardiosis can mimic tuberculosis or malignancy with sweats and weight loss.
Systemic inflammation and chronic infection produce malaise and fatigue.
Delayed pulmonary or disseminated disease can cause anorexia and weight loss.
Leukocytosis may occur with active suppurative infection, although counts can be normal in some hosts.
Neutrophilic response often accompanies abscess-forming disease.
CRP rises with pulmonary, CNS, cutaneous, or disseminated inflammatory burden.
Procalcitonin may be low or modest despite invasive nocardiosis; marked elevation suggests coinfection or severe bacterial sepsis.
Brain abscess is the core imaging expression of CNS nocardiosis.
Untreated or recurrent abscesses enlarge over time and often require drainage when large.
Nocardial brain abscesses usually present as ring-enhancing lesions that mimic metastases, tuberculosis, or fungal abscess.
Disseminated nocardiosis can cause multiple CNS lesions.
Headache is common with mass effect, inflammation, or raised intracranial pressure.
Nausea and vomiting can reflect intracranial mass effect or posterior fossa disease.
Large, recurrent, or posterior fossa abscesses can cause altered consciousness.
Focal parenchymal abscesses can produce motor, sensory, gait, cranial nerve, or cerebellar deficits.
Cortical abscesses can irritate cortex and provoke seizures.
Abscess-associated inflammation and mass effect produce vasogenic edema.
Cutaneous nocardiosis can present with papules, pustules, nodules, ulcers, or draining lesions.
Nocardia can form localized soft-tissue abscesses or draining nodules.
Clinically disseminated nocardiosis involves at least two noncontiguous organ sites or bloodstream spread.
Bacteremia is uncommon but indicates severe dissemination in compromised hosts.
Severe pulmonary nocardiosis can progress to respiratory failure and ARDS physiology.
Large or posterior fossa abscesses with edema can cause life-threatening mass effect.
Inadequate activity, insufficient duration, or retained abscess cavities increase recurrence.
Severe systemic inflammation and sepsis-like illness raise short-term mortality.
Respiratory failure from severe lung disease can be fatal.
CNS nocardiosis has high mortality, especially in immunocompromised hosts or with delayed active therapy.
Multiorgan dissemination marks high organism burden and poor host control.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: CRP and leukocytosis often rise together with systemic inflammatory burden, but discordance is common in immunosuppressed hosts.
Increasing pulmonary infiltrate burden can worsen oxygenation.
Suppurative nodules can cavitate over time.
Worsening hypoxemia raises respiratory failure and ARDS hazard.
Brain abscess with inflammation or mass effect commonly produces headache.
Larger abscesses tend to create greater edema and mass effect.
Edema and mass effect drive herniation risk.
CNS involvement is a major mortality pathway in nocardiosis.
Multiorgan dissemination indicates poor host control and higher fatality.
Active, prolonged, susceptible therapy reduces recurrence risk.
Undrained abscesses or retained infected collections increase relapse.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: TMP-SMX should not be assumed active without susceptibility support because Nocardia species vary.
Severe allergy or intolerance may require desensitization or a non-sulfonamide regimen.
CNS disease usually requires prolonged CNS-active therapy and often combination induction.

side_effects.interpretation: TMP component can increase potassium, especially with kidney disease or interacting drugs.
Creatinine can rise from tubular secretion effects or true kidney injury.

treatments.context_specific_role: Susceptibility-dependent systemic and CNS-active agent that lowers organism survival and relapse pressure when tolerated and active.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Carbapenems are commonly used in induction combinations for severe CNS or disseminated disease when active.

side_effects.interpretation: Carbapenem neurotoxicity is uncommon but relevant in renal impairment or CNS disease.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rapid parenteral active-coverage component for severe, CNS, or disseminated nocardiosis when susceptibility supports use.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Amikacin has broad in vitro Nocardia activity and can add early bactericidal pressure when active.
Kidney disease or transplant graft risk can make aminoglycoside toxicity unacceptable.

side_effects.interpretation: Aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity can threaten kidney function or transplant graft reserve.

treatments.context_specific_role: Short-course induction component for severe or disseminated disease when renal toxicity risk is acceptable.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Linezolid activity against many Nocardia isolates and CNS penetration make it useful when susceptibility supports it.
Baseline cytopenia raises risk from prolonged linezolid myelosuppression.

side_effects.interpretation: Linezolid-associated thrombocytopenia is a major prolonged-treatment limitation.
Anemia can occur with prolonged linezolid.

treatments.context_specific_role: CNS-penetrating active agent or sulfonamide alternative when susceptibility and hematologic tolerance allow.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Cephalosporin activity is species- and isolate-dependent.
CNS disease should not rely on uncertain cephalosporin activity without susceptibility data and adequate companion therapy.

side_effects.interpretation: Main treatment risk is microbiologic inactivity rather than a distinctive disease-axis toxicity.

treatments.context_specific_role: Susceptibility-dependent parenteral companion or step-down component for selected isolates.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: CNS disease usually requires stronger induction and prolonged combination before oral continuation.
Tetracycline role depends on confirmed activity and clinical stability.

side_effects.interpretation: Gastrointestinal intolerance can limit long oral therapy.

treatments.context_specific_role: Oral continuation or alternative component after stabilization when susceptibility and host context are favorable.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Large CNS abscesses often need aspiration or excision for decompression and diagnosis.
Small, improving lesions without mass effect may be managed medically.

side_effects.interpretation: Neurosurgical intervention can carry procedure-related neurologic risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Source control and diagnostic intervention for large, recurrent, mass-effect, cutaneous, or refractory abscesses.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: There is no direct host-restoration effect when iatrogenic immunosuppression is not a driver.
Dissemination signals poor host control, making feasible immunosuppression reduction more valuable.

side_effects.interpretation: Net mortality can rise if rejection or severe underlying disease flare outweighs infection control.

treatments.context_specific_role: Host-control intervention for transplant, steroid, biologic, or chemotherapy contexts when competing disease risks allow tapering.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises invasive pulmonary disease, dissemination, CNS involvement, relapse, drug interaction burden, and mortality.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Transplant and multi-drug immunosuppression directly weaken cell-mediated control.
Dissemination is enriched in immunocompromised hosts.
Poor host control and comorbidity raise fatality.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises invasive disease and may blunt fever or CRP while allowing severe tissue infection.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Steroids and biologics reduce cell-mediated immunity relevant to Nocardia control.
Inflammatory markers can be partially suppressed.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises pulmonary nocardiosis probability and lowers oxygenation reserve.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Structural lung disease is a recognized pulmonary nocardiosis context.
Underlying lung disease lowers respiratory reserve.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises pulmonary, CNS, and disseminated disease probability.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Reduced cellular immunity is central to invasive nocardiosis susceptibility.
Poor immune containment promotes spread beyond the primary site.

present.trajectory_modulation: Modestly raises susceptibility and worsens treatment toxicity constraints.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Kidney disease changes TMP-SMX, carbapenem, and aminoglycoside safety.
Baseline kidney disease shifts creatinine independent of nocardiosis.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises cutaneous inoculation probability and supports Nocardia when pulmonary or skin lesions are otherwise nonspecific.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Nocardia is environmental and commonly associated with soil or dust exposure.
Traumatic inoculation specifically enriches cutaneous disease.

present.trajectory_modulation: Allows progression, CNS spread, abscess enlargement, and relapse; this is a disease-course modifier rather than a prior-only risk.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Incorrect initial therapy or missing susceptibility data can fail to control Nocardia.
Recurrent CNS abscesses often reflect delayed recognition or inadequate active therapy.

present.trajectory_modulation: Does not define the disease leaf but shifts prognosis, treatment duration, source-control need, and mortality.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: CNS and disseminated disease are major mortality pathways.
Large or recurrent abscesses often need drainage or excision.

supportive_care: Notify the microbiology laboratory when nocardiosis is suspected so cultures are held long enough and branching, weakly acid-fast organisms are not dismissed as contaminants.
Do not rely on culture/speciation/PCR as ordinary presentation evidence in case ranking; use them as confirmatory findings and treatment-context inputs.
Obtain chest CT when pulmonary symptoms, nodules, cavitation, recurrent pneumonia, or malignancy-like imaging is present.
Screen for CNS disease with brain MRI or CT when nocardiosis is severe, disseminated, immunocompromised, neurologically symptomatic, or pulmonary disease has no clear alternative explanation.
Obtain species identification and susceptibility testing because TMP-SMX, carbapenem, ceftriaxone, amikacin, fluoroquinolone, and other activity varies by isolate.
Treat severe pulmonary, CNS, or disseminated disease with active combination induction while awaiting susceptibility and clinical response.
Plan prolonged therapy; CNS or disseminated disease usually requires many months and often at least a year of follow-up or treatment depending on host and radiographic response.
Drain or excise large, mass-effect, recurrent, cutaneous, or refractory abscesses when technically feasible and coordinate with neurosurgery, interventional radiology, or surgery.
Monitor CBC, creatinine, potassium, liver tests, drug levels where relevant, and neurologic symptoms during prolonged therapy.
Review immunosuppression, transplant medications, and drug interactions; reduce immunosuppression only when graft or underlying disease risk allows.
Assess for relapse with serial clinical and imaging follow-up, especially when CNS disease, immunosuppression, retained abscess cavity, or initial inactive therapy was present.
quality_notes: No treatment-ranking label fields are used.
The only derived_hazard axis is mortality_hazard_in_D-NOCARDIOSIS.
Culture, speciation, PCR, and susceptibility axes are treatment-context or confirmatory concepts; case files should not duplicate them as ordinary presentation observations.
